rows.heading: Lighting
rows.fuel_or_tech: Street lighting - sodium high pressure - new

notes.Note 1: This table shows how primary energy is allocated through the energy system to final consumption and other uses. Within this table the primary energy total includes non-energy use. Final consumption is further divided into useful and rejected energy.
notes.Note 2: Heat pump useful energy includes ambient heat captured from the environment. This is additional to recorded energy consumption; therefore, useful plus rejected energy exceeds final consumption by the ambient-heat amount.
notes.Note 3: Useful and rejected energy are modelled estimates calculated by applying assumed efficiencies to allocated consumption. See Tables W2 and W3.
notes.Note 4: Total useful energy is the sum of useful energy from final consumption and 50% of energy industry use.
notes.Note 5: Total rejected energy is the sum of rejected energy from final consumption, transformation, losses and the remaining 50% of energy industry use.
notes.Note 6: End-use efficiency estimates are updated where desk research identifies data sources indicating that efficiency values have changed. Not all values were updated between 2017 and 2025.
notes.Note 7: This shows a counterfactual scenario where the end use efficiency assumptions are unchanged from earlier versions of this analysis. Therefore any changes reflect these updated assumptions, and are not necessarily indicative of real-world savings due to improved efficiencies.

identity.rule: useful = consumption × efficiency; rejected = max(0, consumption − useful); ambient heat = max(0, useful − consumption)
